(3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. The rider's only routing-related message was Chat #1 at 17:33 — 'Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way? Just need 2 minutes' — which names no location and asks for a brief stop, not a route change; the driver's one-word 'Sure' at 17:34 accepts a stop, not a diversion, so the consent reaches at most a stop and does not exempt the segment.

The driver did not tell the rider which 7-Eleven he would use; the first and only mention of a specific store is his post-trip written statement ('I went to the one I know') at F12, which is a claim made after the fact and not consent from the rider, and the stop itself was stationary 4 min 10 s at 4918 m from the pickup, 5158 m from the drop-off, off both the pickup and the drop-off route.

The rider is entitled to a partial refund of the unexempted detour mileage, computed from the fare facts as the excess-distance rate: the unexempted segment added 4.89 km (F4) at $1.4102/km (F5), i.e. $6.8957, rounded to $6.90, while the waiting component is to be handled separately.

The metered waiting charge of $1.19 (4.6 min × $0.26/min) is billed for the in-trip stop at an off-route 7-Eleven; on a metered taxi the waiting unit follows the meter (RD-3(c)), so this item is not refundable on its own, but it is further proof that the stop, not any traffic cause, consumed the trip time.

The dispute is not a bare disagreement on duration: the trip took 36.7 min against an estimated 21.8 min (+14.9 min) and covered 20.9 km against 15.5 km (+5.4 km, +35%), which corroborates the detour rather than routine traffic on the optimal route.
